rationale: bugs_open/340, filed 2026-08-21 at the council's own direction when bugs_closed/215 closed (the architecture seat objected that the gap was out-of-scope prose with no tracked item and would be 're-discovered by another incident the same way this one was'). Closing it properly rather than leaving it. THE DEFECT: reconcilePlanWithRealised builds a preservation set (build_status in deployed/needs_rebuild, or the site's first plan) and then REPLACES its input with it — 'existingPages = preserved'. Every index downstream is built over that subset. So a realised row that is neither deployed nor needs_rebuild, on a site that already has a current plan, is invisible to realisedByName, realisedByURL and all three twin-identity keys, and therefore unreachable by every route that mints identity_authority='realised'. The pages upsert, however, collides on (site_id, name) whatever build_status says — so the write path re-derives the name through CanonicalisePage, misses, and INSERTs the twin the same-name stamp exists to prevent. honour_realised_identity cannot help, whatever the site opted into. THE FIX is 340's candidate 2, not its candidate 1, and the deviation is deliberate and stated in the file. Candidate 1 (widen all four identity maps) couples identity to composition: the twin layers snap the WHOLE entry through snapPlanPageOntoRealised, which carries the realised composition, so widening their input would let a plan entry inherit the empty composition of a page nobody has built yet. That is a different change needing its own population measurement. The same-name stamp writes identity fields and never touches sections, so widening ONLY what it can see is safe in exactly the way widening the snap layers is not. So: one new name index built over every realised row, consulted by the stamp alone, on the arm where the preserved index misses. INERTNESS IS UNCHANGED, which is the whole safety argument and the thing to attack. No new field is written that was not already written by the stamp shipped in corr 27cccfbd: identity_authority (no reader outside realisedIdentityOf, whose two call sites are both inside 'if identityPolicy.HonourRealisedIdentity' — enumerated exhaustively in that round), url (both write surfaces derive and overwrite it when not honouring), and page_type (written back only where it already equals the writers' own firstNonEmptyField derivation, which is what the stamp's type-equality precondition guarantees). No new config key, no writer edit, no new DB read, no change to the twin layers, no change to any composition pass. A SITE THAT HAS OPTED IN sees this only for rows the preservation rules excluded — which is the population that was silently minting twins. THE RESIDUE IS STATED, NOT SILENTLY CLOSED: when NOTHING is preserved the function still takes its from-scratch early return and hands the plan back untouched, so a site on which no page is deployed or needs_rebuild keeps the pre-340 behaviour. Every page on such a site is unbuilt, so that twin is a twin of nothing anyone has served; and the early return is what makes a from-scratch build cheap. Pinned by its own test so the limitation cannot be closed by accident. POPULATION [MEASURED 2026-08-21, live DB]: 40 unpreserved active pages across 13 domains on sites with a current plan, of which ZERO would actually be renamed by a re-derivation today — against 64 across 9 domains for the whole active population, so the predicate discriminates and the measurement could have come out otherwise. The defect is live in mechanism and empty in fact, which is precisely why it needed fixing before the population became non-empty rather than after.

plan.summary: bugs_open/340: give the same-name identity stamp a name index built over EVERY realised row, not just the preserved subset, so a page the preservation rules exclude can no longer have its identity re-derived into a twin. Identity only — the twin layers and every composition pass are untouched, and flag-off inertness is unchanged.

edits.rationale: Build the identity index BEFORE 'existingPages = preserved' discards the rest. Placed and commented so the next reader sees why it is a separate map rather than a widening of the existing ones: the preservation set answers 'whose COMPOSITION must a re-plan not redesign?', and who owns a page's NAME is a different question that has no reason to inherit the narrower answer. The comment also records the from-scratch residue at the early return, so the limitation lives where someone would otherwise re-introduce it.

The consuming arm. Pass B2's existing block becomes an if/else: when the preserved name index misses, consult the wider one and stamp IDENTITY ONLY — deliberately no composition reconciliation against a row the preservation rules excluded. The preserved arm is byte-unchanged, so every existing Pass B2 contract test still exercises the same path.

Three tests, each with a mutation that kills it — run, not predicted. ReachesAnUnpreservedRealisedRow is 340 in one page (a deployed page so the early return is not taken, plus a 'planned' row the planner names verbatim). UnpreservedRowGetsIdentityButNOTComposition pins the restriction the safety argument rests on, by giving the unpreserved row a composition that must not reach the plan. FromScratchBuildIsStillUntouched pins the stated residue so it cannot be closed by accident. MUTATIONS: wider index not consulted -> first test red; wider index built over 'preserved' instead of every row (the subtle wrong fix) -> first test red; unpreserved arm also imposes composition -> second test red; from-scratch early return removed -> third test red.

Close-out on the bug's own file: which candidate was taken and WHY candidate 1 was not (the identity/composition coupling), the mutation table, the population re-measured on the day, and the residue restated as a stated limitation with the test that pins it. Registered in the same commit per the 2026-07-28 ordering exemption.

grounded_in: bugs_open/340, filed at the council's direction: the architecture seat's advisory objection on corr 27cccfbd — 'The preservation-set hole (unbuilt realised page never enters realisedByName) is named as out-of-scope prose only, with no bug filed — it will be re-discovered by another incident the same way this one was, unless it gets its own tracked item now.'

v3_site_actions.go reconcilePlanWithRealised: 'if len(preserved) == 0 { return llmPages, counts }' followed by 'existingPages = preserved' — the two lines that make every downstream index see the subset only.

realisedPageCompositionIsPreserved: build_status in {deployed, needs_rebuild}, false when the column is absent; noCurrentPlanFlag: true only on a site's first plan after adoption. Together these are the exclusion this fix routes around for identity.

site_db_actions.go upsertPage: 'INSERT INTO pages ... ON CONFLICT (site_id, name) DO UPDATE' — keyed on name and nothing else, which is why an excluded row still collides and why re-deriving its name INSERTs a twin.

site_identity_policy.go realisedIdentityOf — the sole reader of identity_authority, called at exactly two sites, both immediately preceded by 'if identityPolicy.HonourRealisedIdentity' (enumerated exhaustively in the corr 27cccfbd round at the editquality seat's request).

bugs_open/340's own candidate list: '(1) Give the identity routes a wider input than the composition routes ... Cost: the identity routes would then fire for pages the reconciler currently ignores entirely, so the flag-off inertness argument has to be re-made for that wider set ... and snapPlanPageOntoRealised carries composition, so the split has to be real rather than nominal. (2) Stamp identity for unpreserved same-name rows only — the narrow version of (1) ... Smaller blast radius, closes only the same-name door, leaves the twin layers as they are.'

bugs_open/340's own warning against a careless widening: 'an unpreserved page is often an unbuilt one, and the twin layers already REFUSE a never-shipped stem twin on the stated ground that a shared stem is not evidence two rows are one page. Any widening has to keep that refusal, or it trades a phantom for a wrong snap.' This fix does not touch the twin layers at all.

[MEASURED 2026-08-21, live DB] 40 unpreserved active pages across 13 domains on sites with a current plan (adversecreditmortgage.co.uk 19, then 3 or fewer each), of which 0 carry a role-prefixed page_type whose name lacks the prefix — i.e. zero would actually be renamed today. Against 64 across 9 domains for the whole active population, so the predicate discriminates.

[MEASURED by mutation 2026-08-21] wider index not consulted -> TestReconcile_SameNameStamp_ReachesAnUnpreservedRealisedRow red; index built over 'preserved' instead of every row -> same test red; unpreserved arm also imposing composition -> TestReconcile_SameNameStamp_UnpreservedRowGetsIdentityButNOTComposition red; from-scratch early return removed -> TestReconcile_SameNameStamp_FromScratchBuildIsStillUntouched red.
